kernel_of_truth: Three real things sit under the dome's eclipse claims. Eclipses do disturb ground magnetometers, and on 2026-08-12 the raw H at the dome's stations really was 13-19 nT low. The dome's quiet-day precondition is good practice; its Boulder statistic is well defined and exactly reproducible, and this day failed it. And across the dome's stations the eclipse-window Z residuals do increase northward in its FSF order, more than on any of 19 ordinary days. A fourth point: the PRED-095 card's own falsifier did not fire. None of that saves the claims: ordinary days produce the same raw H and meet both of the card's bands; the card's -17.8 nT was testable and absent at the lags its own "during totality" admits; the dome's named Z component shows the latitude ordering at about half the formula's -10.9-baseline size and far below its x1.672 size; the contact-phase signature it calls ECM-unique is absent where it would have stood out; and a sunset eclipse under standard physics can also produce larger effects where the Sun stood higher - in the north - though we have not shown that it does here. Being right about the ordering does not favour dome physics. A void test is not a confirmation, and the dome's own live scoreboard still reads PENDING.

anticipated_objections.objection: Dome defender: "By its own pre-registered falsification line PRED-095 was not falsified. You overrode the proponent's registration with your own rule."
anticipated_objections.response: Correct that its own falsifier did not fire; we say so in the headline, the result, the note and dome_favourable_findings. But we hold our own registration to the same override: our B1-M-001 band was "met" by its registered metric and is reported falsified as-if under DR-1. Using "own lines" for the dome and DR-1 for us, or the reverse, is the one option we rule out. Under Option B both stay pending.

anticipated_objections.objection: Defender: "'During totality' says when to measure, not how fast the ionosphere responds. A lagged response is still measured during totality."
anticipated_objections.response: Then the literal measurement is the raw H at totality (R1), and on R1 -17.8 nT is below the 3-sigma detection threshold (24-27 nT) - untested, not confirmed. Its claim band is met on 1/19 and 2/25 ordinary days. And at tau 30 the label is the same after the control discount. The outcome does not hinge on the lag bound; it hinges on whether a non-eclipsed control discount applies, which we apply to both sides.

anticipated_objections.objection: Our side (curmudgeon-style): "The CTL-1 0.75 factor and the 0.8 power floor were chosen now."
anticipated_objections.response: Yes (honest_limits). The 0.75 factor reproduces exactly the three discounts rev4 stated in words before it was chosen, discounts nothing else, and is applied to both sides by the same code; the power floor is met at 0.95-1.00 for every card cell, so neither choice decides an outcome.

anticipated_objections.objection: Defender: "Your lag-aware test still rejects x1.672 only because you cut the lag window at 30 min."
anticipated_objections.response: The window is the dome's own: "Z minimum within 30 minutes of maximum", "umbra-locked", "during totality". At a 60-min lag the lag-matched weakest variant is 2.87, mismatched 1.21 - reported, not hidden. A response 60 min late would itself contradict the dome's timing claims.

anticipated_objections.objection: Standard-physics side: "You withdrew 'what standard physics expects'. Does that weaken the review?"
anticipated_objections.response: It removes a claim we had not earned. The sign of a standard response depends on position relative to the path (Meza 2022), and we did not compute the thin-sheet geometry. The verdicts on the dome's registrations do not rest on it; only the description of the residual changes.
